ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZlu_7w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDMSnQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 87, "title": "Correct successful V30MZ DIV/IDIV timing without double-counting operand transfers", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `e08ee15715a9380d842623c72f6dfc00852d27f7`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:1260` charges division 24/32 residual clocks by width, regardless of signedness or success. Successful arithmetic therefore advances timers, raster and audio too far. Existing division tests preserve these charges.

For two-byte register instructions in internal RAM, calculated current→required totals are:

| Form | Bytes | Clocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Byte DIV | `F6 F3` | 26→17 |
| Byte IDIV | `F6 FB` | 26→19 |
| Word DIV | `F7 F3` | 34→25 |
| Word IDIV | `F7 FB` | 34→26 |

These are source-derived expectations, not executed observations. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Correct successful byte/word DIV and IDIV timing through ordinary decoding. Preserve quotient/remainder, complete FLAGS, operand sampling, multiplication history and continuation. Include necessary CPU tests, an original timing cartridge, native/browser consumers and accounting documentation.

Separate successful timing from fault timing so this correction cannot silently change exceptional behavior.

## Context

The clean local checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 86 closed entry titles were checked. [PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/pull/86) explicitly leaves division timing separate.

The [NEC V30MZ preliminary manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Appendix A, printed pp. 73/77–78, gives unsigned byte/word register costs 15/23 and signed costs 17/24. Memory forms add one normal aligned source transfer. Conditions include completed decoding, no waits/holds, aligned words and qualified effective addressing. Since the bus already charges the operand read, use the register costs as residuals; retain actual fetch, alignment and wait charges once. This is an explicit inference for the existing serialized scheduler.

Correction record: replace the former AI-authored requirement to preserve width-only 24/32 residuals with that accounting. Earlier [#47](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/47), [#49](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/49) and [#65](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/65) architectural acceptance remains applicable. Record further evidence-based corrections with the old assumption, corrected requirement, source and rationale; preserve valid acceptance without introducing an approval gate.

Full prefetch/pipeline timing and effective-address hazards remain separate gaps. The inspected [WSTimingTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSTimingTest/blob/025e606fc3b6615160ffdae485d992ffcad0c024/README.md) explicitly limits interpretation of aggregate loop results. [WSCPUTest](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) identifies exceptional division discrepancies; this successful-timing task does not establish fault classification, flags, continuation or exact fault timing as hardware-correct.

[Saved #85 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/e08ee15715a9380d842623c72f6dfc00852d27f7/docs/issue-85-validation.md) reports 312 workspace tests, complete production Chromium suites and Coordinator criterion review passing. Relevant tests and tooling were inspected; no application builds or tests were run during this investigation.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Before changing production charges, add independent literal timing/full-state vectors for all four successful forms and record actual baseline failures followed by corrected passes. Require the register totals above. For unprefixed `[BX]` in internal RAM, byte/even-word totals are respectively 18/20/26/27; odd word operands add one. Expectations must not call production timing helpers.
- [ ] Preserve independent quotient/remainder/full-FLAGS assertions under contrasting incoming flags, zero and nonzero remainders, odd/even quotients, unsigned high-word dividends and signed operand combinations. Use unambiguous successful signed boundaries ±127/±32767. Retain valid AL/AH/AX/DX aliases, unchanged unrelated state/source memory, exact IP, following instructions and multiplication-history independence. Unsigned byte DIV with AH as divisor must remain a fault regression; it cannot succeed.
- [ ] Verify exact fetch/source accounting for registers and mapped RAM/SRAM/ROM, even/odd operands and fetches, DS/SS defaults, overrides, displacements, wrapping and relevant mapping boundaries. Cover live A0 `00/04/08/0C`, existing SRAM waits and supported mixed segment/BUSLOCK prefixes. Assert one source read and no source writes; preserve REP diagnostics.
- [ ] Keep successful and fault charge selection distinct. Add discriminating zero-divisor/overflow regressions preserving current fault costs, saved frame, register/history retention and diagnostics as baseline policies. Document their unresolved hardware accuracy; do not apply successful timing to faults or expand into exception-semantics changes.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations: Mono `00`; Color and SwanCrystal `00/80/C0/E0`, including live returns to `00`. Through normal `Machine::run_frame`, check representative divisions crossing raster/frame boundaries, exact elapsed clocks, timer/raster/frame progression, stereo sample production and absence of an extra continuation instruction. Preserve IF shadows, TF/IRQ delivery and actual IRET continuation with separately accounted entry costs, REP/HALT and capability-gated GDMA/SDMA reservations.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 timing cartridge using existing fixture tooling, plus independent native and production Chromium/Wasm consumers integrated into existing suites. Cover all four forms with register and even/odd memory sources. Reload valid operands per repetition. Derive absolute timer bounds from emitted instructions; check CPU-written results, full FLAGS, execution counts, continuation and fresh completion. Re-poison retained observations before each of two boots. Run identical final probe bytes with former and corrected charges in both consumers, collecting all model/mode and boot observations before reporting timing failures.
- [ ] Audit existing division-dependent intervals and scheduler/trap assertions, including the current 51-clock byte-division-plus-trap expectations. Recalculate affected budgets independently; preserve unrelated assertions, historical reports and prior fixture/demo bytes without widening tolerances. Retain prior CPU/timing acceptance, firmware-free startup, three-model gates, LCD/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, DMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM, both EEPROM controllers, RTC, browser save integrity and ownership/provenance.
- [ ] Before merge, Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm` and `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the final production build. Update hardware/accounting/provenance documentation and record tested source/artifact identities, actual failures/passes, resolutions and uncertainty. Coordinator reviews every checkbox against the final diff and evidence and resolves blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Additional independent software vectors, other browser engines and lawfully available workloads. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are optional and unperformed here. Proprietary ROMs/firmware, device identities and human sign-off are unnecessary for mandatory acceptance. Original-probe success establishes bounded behavior, not commercial-catalog readiness.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
